# Case study: IK tracking

Put the pieces together. A site (or EE link) tracks a target pose:

1. FK → EE pose ([Forward kinematics](forward-kinematics.qmd#forward-kinematics), `link8` in the demos).
2. Pose error → `dq` via `make_ik("dls")` ([Useful Patterns](useful-patterns.qmd#useful-patterns)).
3. Write joints or actuator targets; `step` ([State I/O](state-sensors-and-actuators.qmd#state-sensors-and-actuators)).
4. Loop ([Simulation loop](the-simulation-loop.qmd#the-simulation-loop)).

Same `IKConfig` / registry as [Useful Patterns](useful-patterns.qmd#useful-patterns). Success is residual vs time, not a screenshot. Python patterns (registry, `@register`) and type tooling: [References — Python / PEPs](references.qmd#peps-style-packaging-typing).

## What exists today

| Piece | Where |
|---|---|
| NumPy IK solvers + registry | `src/robotics/ik/`, `scripts/ik_controllers.py`, `scripts/train.py` |
| Load Piper + state I/O + step | `scripts/mujoco_robot_demo.py`, `scripts/motrix_robot_demo.py` |
| Damped IK debug plot | `scripts/debug_ik.py`, `notebooks/inspect_ik.ipynb` |

A single end-to-end **sim + IK tracking** script (MuJoCo and Motrix backends, optional Motrix built-in IK) is the natural next increment — wire `make_ik("dls")` into the lockstep loop from the robot demos, log $\lVert \text{residual} \rVert$ each tick.

Until that script lands, combine the demos manually: FK readout from section 2 of `mujoco_robot_demo.py`, Jacobian/residual from `scripts/train.py`, write `ctrl` or `qpos` as in section 3–4.
